questions.question: You arrive to find 4 workers collapsed near a loading dock, no trauma. Per Step 1-2-3:
options: D. Do not approach; withdraw, report, isolate
questions.rationale: Three or more casualties without explanation = do not approach.

questions.question: ERG pages listing materials by 4-digit ID number are:
questions.rationale: Yellow = ID number; Blue = name; Orange = guide; Green = distances.

questions.question: In the NFPA 704 diamond, the blue section indicates:
A placard with hazard class 8 indicates:
Which PPE level uses an air-purifying respirator?
questions.rationale: Level C uses APR/PAPR — requires a known agent and adequate oxygen.

questions.question: The most effective initial decon step is:
Wet decon is especially indicated for:
options: B. Vapor-only exposure with no symptoms
C. All patients regardless of exposure
D. Caustic exposures or visible liquid contamination
questions.rationale: Dry decon suffices for most; go wet for caustics/liquids/symptoms.

questions.question: A critical contaminated patient with arterial bleeding in the decon line should:
options: B. Receive LSIs (tourniquet) from protected staff during rapid gross decon
C. Wait at the end of the line
D. Skip decon and be transported
questions.rationale: Combine LSIs with rapid decon — never transport contaminated.

questions.question: Which statement about Level C PPE is TRUE?
options: D. Requires a known agent and adequate oxygen
questions.rationale: APRs filter ambient air; they don't supply oxygen.

questions.question: ERG green pages tell you:
options: C. Initial isolation and protective action distances for toxic-inhalation hazards
